title: The password rules' author publicly recanted them
body: Bill Burr wrote the 2003 NIST guidance demanding mixed characters and frequent changes, then in 2017 told the Wall Street Journal he regretted it: users responded with predictable patterns like Password1! and seasonal rotations. NIST's revised 800-63B favours length, screening against breached lists, and no routine expiry. Security theatre loses slowly to evidence.
source_hint: NIST SP 800-63B (2017); WSJ interview with Burr
